best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2: stay in the gbdt family but move to a heavily regularised, low-capacity hist_gbdt so the ranking stops being spent on memorised noise. Concretely: max_iter 600 at learning_rate 0.03 (same effective budget, much smaller steps), max_leaf_nodes 8 with max_depth 4, min_samples_leaf 60, l2_regularization 20.0, and max_features 0.6 for column subsampling. Keep preprocessing exactly as attempt 1 (impute 'none' so the trees split on NaN natively across the 60 missing columns including expected_num_interested_in_me at 78.5%, no scaling, no missingness columns) and keep class_weight='balanced' so the default predict() cut stays near the balanced point. This isolates capacity as the only changed axis: read roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against attempt 1's 0.8598 / 0.6049 / 0.7922 and train_val_gap against 0.2752 to see whether shrinking capacity raised the ranking. early_stopping stays false so all 5,026 train rows are used and the score stays comparable.

critic.evidence: hist_gbdt scored balanced_accuracy 0.7248 (95% CI 0.6969~0.7527) against the bar 0.8882 — a shortfall of 0.1634. train_balanced_accuracy = 1.0 with train_val_gap = 0.2752 and train_f1 = 1.0: 400 iterations at lr 0.06 with 31 leaves and min_samples_leaf 20 memorised all 5,026 training rows, so capacity is being spent on noise rather than ranking. The ranking did move off the baseline (roc_auc 0.8598 vs 0.8419, pr_auc 0.6049 vs 0.5751, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7922 vs the baseline ceiling 0.7649), so the family swap was not wasted, but the ceiling is still 0.0960 short of the bar. On the operating-point axis cut_headroom is only 0.0674 against 0.1634 still to go — 41% at most from any cut/class_weight move, and recall 0.5254 vs specificity 0.9243 says 'balanced' has already been applied and is still cutting conservatively. Since the ranking ceiling is where 59% of the remaining distance sits, and train is saturated at 1.0, the binding problem this attempt shows is unregularised capacity inside a family that has only been tried once — not an exhausted family (only 1 family tried, so no plateau) and not the threshold.
critic.direction: Stay in hist_gbdt but kill the memorisation that is capping the ranking: cut capacity and raise regularisation hard (shallower/coarser trees, much stronger l2 and larger leaves, lower learning rate with the same budget) while leaving preprocessing and class_weight exactly as they were, so the next row attributes any change in roc_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut to capacity alone.

critic.evidence: Attempt 2 scored balanced_accuracy 0.7778 (95% CI 0.7510~0.8021) against the bar 0.8882 — still 0.1104 short. The paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0529 (95% CI +0.0290~+0.0771, P 1.000), so the regularisation did resolve as a gain, but it bought almost none of it on the ranking axis: roc_auc 0.8598→0.8604, pr_auc 0.6049→0.5925 (down), and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7922→0.7891 (down). The entire +0.0529 was the default cut moving — recall 0.5254→0.7355, specificity 0.9243→0.8200 — and that lever is now exhausted: cut_headroom is 0.0113 against 0.1104 still to go, i.e. at most 10% of the remaining distance, with recall 0.7355 vs specificity 0.8200 nearly crossed. train_val_gap fell 0.2752→0.1036 with train_balanced_accuracy 1.0→0.8813, so the memorisation diagnosis is now closed: capacity is no longer the binding constraint and re-tuning hist_gbdt's capacity knobs cannot repay 0.1104. Two hist_gbdt attempts have plateaued at a ranking ceiling of 0.7891~0.7922, which is itself above the baseline's 0.7649 ceiling but 0.099 under the bar; the goal's own note says the required KS is 0.7764 vs baseline 0.5297, so 90% of what is left is ranking. No hyperparameters were dropped (dropped_hyperparams empty) and cost is trivial (8.35 s of a 600 s budget), so nothing is resource-limited. 3 iterations remain.
critic.direction: Stop tuning hist_gbdt — its ranking ceiling has sat at 0.789~0.792 across two very different capacity points while the cut lever is spent (cut_headroom 0.0113) — and spend the next attempt on a different family's ranking, fitting xgboost (the only other family that also takes impute 'none', so preprocessing stays untouched and the Δ is attributable to the family alone) with moderate depth, strong shrinkage and column/row subsampling plus scale_pos_weight at the class ratio.

critic.evidence: extra_trees scored balanced_accuracy 0.7409 (95% CI 0.7155~0.7729) against the bar 0.8882 — 0.1473 short, and the paired Δ vs iteration 2 is -0.0369 (95% CI -0.0583~-0.0118, P(better) 0.000), a resolved regression. One more family off the same list cannot cover 0.0960; only 0.0306 of cut_headroom (21% of the remaining 0.1473) is purchasable at all with the levers the executor has. dropped_hyperparams is empty and cost is trivial (5.3 s train, 7.9 s wall of 600 s), so nothing is resource-bound. critic.direction: Stop swapping families — with 2 iterations left and the ranking shortfall (0.0960 at best cut) five times the whole span the two families tried have covered, spend the next attempt inside the best-known ranking (iteration 2's hist_gbdt with impute 'none') and buy back the only measurable piece left, the ~0.011 operating-point headroom, by nudging the positive class weight slightly below 'balanced' (recall 0.7355 < specificity 0.8200 says the cut is fine but the weight point is a touch conservative on specificity... it is recall that is lower, so raise positive weight modestly) — i.e. refit iteration 2 exactly, changing only class_weight to an explicit {"0": 1, "1": 6} so recall and specificity meet, and keep every other lever fixed so the row is attributable.
